newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba - 1996 deficit to weight on Germany making EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba - 1996 deficit to weight on Germany making EMU.

text.p: Germany's chances of meeting criteria for entry into the European currency will depend on how Bonn overcomes pressures from record unemployment that weighed on the 1996 budget, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday.

The German central bank said in its monthly report for February that budget developments would be influenced more strongly by the fact that high deficits for social spending in 1996 must be evened out.

Germany's federal budget deficit surged to 78.50 billion marks ($46.10 billion) last year from earlier estimates of about 53.50 billion marks as double-digit unemployment rates forced Bonn to pay out unexpected billions of marks in benefits.

The additional spending forced Germany's budget deficit to 3.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1996, well above the Maastricht Treaty criteria requiring a budget deficit below three percent for entry into currency union in 1999.

"The fact that the final 1996 budget deficit was more unfavourable due to weaker tax income and higher unemployment costs than had been imagined when budget plans for 1997 were finalised will also mean pressure on the budget in the current year," the Bundesbank said in the monthly report.
"Whether the estimated budget deficit can be sustained in the final analysis will depend upon to what extent additional burdens can be compensated for," the report said.

The Bundesbank called on Bonn to make every effort possible to rein in spending during the year. It noted the government had upped its 1997 deficit forecast to 2.9 percent from an earlier forecast of 2.5 percent in November 1996.
The German central bank said that budget-saving measures announced in 1996 might help to reduce the deficit and that savings measures would probably be beefed up.
Bonn's current plans call for overall spending to only exceed 1996 levels and for 1997 federal budget spending to rise about 2.5 percent over year-ago levels, the Bundesbank said.

But government officials expect only a modest increase in intake from tax revenues despite prospects for economic growth and higher revenue inflows in the early part of 1997 compared with 1996 when tax reform measures were introduced.
